solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Sorry end for Paul Pogba's Italian course

indicators.note: sorry in the sense of sorry-looking or wretched, so the letters are in a poor, jumbled state

parts.note: taken as written, apostrophe dropped

indicators.note: end for asks for the final letter of the word that follows

parts.note: last letter of Paul

explanation.surface: A footballer's career ending badly, Paul Pogba being a French midfielder who played in Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sorry' rearranges POGBAS into SPAGBO, then L, the end of Paul, follows. Spag bol is British slang for spaghetti bolognese.
explanation.definitionFit: Spaghetti bolognese is a pasta dish of Italian origin, served as a course of a meal.

clue.text: Plastery cup he mixed filler in

indicators.note: mixed means the letters are stirred into a new combination

explanation.surface: A builder mixing plaster in a cup to fill a hole.
explanation.walkthrough: 'filler' suggests plaster for cracks, but here it is someone who fills in.
explanation.definitionFit: A supply teacher stands in for an absent regular teacher, covering their classes temporarily.

clue.text: Young prince holds five records

indicators.note: holds means the name contains the numeral within it

parts.note: Archie is the young son of Prince Harry
V is the Roman numeral for five

explanation.surface: A boy prince clutching five music albums.
explanation.definitionFit: An archive is a collection of historical documents kept as a store of information.

clue.text: Lecturer's sent an invoice for construction project

indicators.note: a lecturer speaks aloud, so this is how the word is pronounced

parts.note: billed means sent a bill or invoice

explanation.surface: A lecturer's invoice for work on a building job.
explanation.definitionFit: A build is a construction job, as in a new-build house or a self-build.

clue.text: Large sea dike affected shore

indicators.note: affected means altered, so the letters change their order

explanation.surface: A large sea wall having an impact on the coastline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shore' looks like a verb meaning support, fitting the dike, but it is the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A lakeside is the edge or bank of a lake, a stretch of waterfront.

clue.text: Married couple's introduction occupying studio, perhaps making this?

definitions.text: Married couple's introduction occupying studio, perhaps making this?

indicators.note: occupying means the letters sit inside the room, filling it

parts.note: a studio is one example of a room, hence the 'perhaps'

indicators.note: introduction means the opening letter of the word

parts.note: first letter of couple

explanation.surface: A film studio shooting a story about husband and wife meeting for the first time.
explanation.walkthrough: As a whole the clue describes what a studio might produce about a couple meeting, so the entire clue doubles as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A romcom is a romantic comedy film, the kind of picture a studio makes about a couple getting together.

clue.text: Racket among equipment for sport

indicators.note: among means set in the middle of the other word

parts.note: a rig is a set of equipment or apparatus
din means a racket, a loud noise

explanation.surface: A tennis racket stored with other sports kit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Racket' suggests the tennis bat, but it means noise.
explanation.definitionFit: Riding, on horseback, is an equestrian pastime and competitive activity.

clue.text: You'd say girl will pull, standing under this?

indicators.note: you'd say signals the words as spoken aloud

parts.note: miss is a girl or young woman; 'll is the contracted form of will; to tow is to pull

explanation.surface: A girl standing under the Christmas sprig is likely to get a kiss.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface plays on 'pull' as British slang for attracting a partner; spoken, 'miss'll tow' sounds like the plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Mistletoe is hung at Christmas, and custom says anyone standing beneath it may be kissed.

clue.text: Section in exam relating to planetary movement

indicators.note: in means the first piece is put inside the second word

parts.note: an oral is a spoken examination
a bit is a part or section

explanation.surface: A part of an astronomy exam about how planets move.
explanation.definitionFit: Orbital describes the path of a planet circling the sun, its orbit.

clue.text: Fed outside shot then arrested

parts.note: a pic is a photograph, a shot
nicked is British slang for arrested by the police

explanation.surface: A news report: someone was fed outside, shot, then arrested.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fed' looks like the police (a US Fed) given the shooting and arrest, but it is the past tense of eat; nicked is British slang for arrested.
explanation.definitionFit: To picnic is to eat a meal out of doors, so having picnicked is having eaten outside.

clue.text: Fortune-teller is returning via Luxembourg

indicators.note: returning means the short word is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: by means via, as in going by Paris
L is the international vehicle code for Luxembourg

explanation.surface: A clairvoyant on her way home travelling through Luxembourg.
explanation.definitionFit: A sibyl was a prophetess of the ancient world, so a woman who foretells the future.

clue.text: Fresh clean pink trousers upset professional soldier

indicators.note: fresh means made new, so the letters are recast
trousers is a verb here, meaning to pocket or take inside

parts.note: coral is a pinkish colour

indicators.note: upset means overturned, so the letters are read in the opposite direction in a down clue

parts.note: pro is short for professional

explanation.surface: Clean pink trousers worn by a soldier, upset by the mess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trousers' looks like clothing but is a verb: CORAL takes in ORP, made when 'upset' turns PRO over.
explanation.definitionFit: A lance corporal is the lowest non-commissioned rank in the British Army, a junior NCO.

clue.text: Island guarded by fat landowner

indicators.note: guarded by means the letter is enclosed and protected within the other word

parts.note: lard is pig fat

explanation.surface: An island protected by a stout aristocrat who owns it.
explanation.walkthrough: A laird is the Scottish term for a landed proprietor.
explanation.definitionFit: A laird is a Scottish lord of an estate, a proprietor of large holdings of property.

clue.text: Snitch disclosed something unique

parts.note: to sing is slang for informing on someone, to snitch
let on means revealed or disclosed

explanation.surface: An informer revealed a one-off secret.
explanation.definitionFit: A singleton is a single individual item, one of a kind with no pair.

clue.text: Reformed Goth does what was promised

indicators.note: reformed means formed again in a new arrangement of the letters

explanation.surface: A goth who has changed their ways keeps their word.
explanation.walkthrough: To deliver the goods is an idiom for doing what was promised.
explanation.definitionFit: The goods, in the idiom 'deliver the goods', are the expected results or the thing undertaken.

clue.text: Company at desks all doing the same work

definitions.text: Company at desks all doing the same work

parts.words: Company at desks all doing the same work
parts.note: musicians in a symphony band sit at music stands called desks, all playing one piece together

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like an office of clerks; in a symphony band a desk is a shared music stand, and the work is a musical composition.
explanation.definitionFit: An orchestra is a company of instrumentalists seated in pairs at desks, performing a single musical work.

clue.text: A dry American general, WWII deputy

parts.note: TT means teetotal, so dry in the sense of not drinking
Robert E. Lee was the Confederate general in the American Civil War

explanation.surface: A teetotal US general who served as second in command in the Second World War.
explanation.walkthrough: Clement Attlee was Churchill's deputy prime minister in the wartime coalition.
explanation.definitionFit: Attlee served as Deputy Prime Minister under Churchill during the war before becoming premier in 1945.

clue.text: Stranger intrudes on the German party over the hill

indicators.note: intrudes on means pushing in between the letters of the other piece

parts.note: der is German for 'the' (masculine)
odder means stranger, more peculiar

explanation.surface: An odd outsider gatecrashing a German political party gathering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'party' is not a gathering but a person, as in 'the guilty party'.
explanation.definitionFit: A dodderer is a feeble, shaky elderly person, someone past their prime.

clue.text: Now curtain's opening late in act one

indicators.note: late in means the letter is shifted to a later position within the phrase

parts.note: the two words run together

indicators.note: opening means the first letter of the word

parts.note: first letter of curtain

explanation.surface: A theatre complaint: the curtain went up late during the first act.
explanation.walkthrough: In ACTONE the C, which is the opening of 'curtain's', sits second; 'late in' moves it to a later spot, just before the final E.
explanation.definitionFit: At once means immediately, right now, without any delay.

clue.text: Roman virgin playing Ludo with Ray

indicators.note: playing means the letters are being toyed with into a new order

explanation.surface: A Roman Catholic nun playing a board game with someone called Ray.
explanation.walkthrough: Ludo is a simple board game, and Roman here means Roman Catholic.
explanation.definitionFit: Our Lady is the Catholic title for the Virgin Mary, mother of Jesus.

clue.text: Defence experts muse without haste

parts.note: the MoD, the UK Ministry of Defence, is the body of defence specialists
Erato is the Greek muse of lyric poetry

explanation.surface: Military specialists pondering a problem slowly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'muse' looks like a verb meaning ponder, but it is one of the nine Muses.
explanation.definitionFit: Moderato is a musical tempo marking meaning at a moderate pace, neither fast nor slow.

clue.text: Greek virgin from Meganisi met Ray on the rebound

indicators.note: on the rebound says the hidden letters are read backwards
from signals the letters are taken out of the run of words that follows

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A Greek maiden on a Greek island meeting someone called Ray after a breakup.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' marks the hidden letters, added as the indicator the draft left out. Meganisi is a small Greek island; 'on the rebound' reads like romance but turns the letters around.
explanation.definitionFit: Artemis was the Greek goddess of the hunt, sworn to perpetual chastity.

clue.text: Tramp exercises in large grassy area

parts.note: to step is to tread or tramp
PE is physical education, school exercises

explanation.surface: A hiker doing workouts while walking across open grassland.
explanation.definitionFit: The steppe is the vast treeless plain of eastern Europe and central Asia.

clue.text: Organise vet as herd brought in to the barn?

indicators.note: organise means put into a new order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A farmer telling the vet to arrange the cattle, with the herd brought into the barn.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the definition as a fanciful description: a crop that is gathered in is taken to the barn.
explanation.definitionFit: A harvested crop has been gathered from the fields and stored, typically in a barn.

clue.text: Use tupperware boxes to get things organised

indicators.note: boxes means the phrase holds the answer within it, like a container

explanation.surface: Kitchen advice: plastic containers will tidy things up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boxes' looks like a noun for the Tupperware, but it is a verb saying the clue words contain the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To set up is to arrange or establish something, putting matters in order.

clue.text: Utter disbelief at fare

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to mock it as unbelievable
second meaning: British slang for food

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like protesting a ticket price; scoff is both a verb of mockery and slang for grub.
explanation.definitionFit: Scoff can mean to jeer derisively and, as a noun, means grub or eatables.

clue.text: Carpet burn

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to carpet someone is to reprimand them severely
second meaning: to scorch or overheat

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests the friction injury, a carpet burn, but the two words are separate senses: to carpet someone is British slang for to reprimand them.
explanation.definitionFit: Roast means to criticise harshly and also to cook or scorch with fierce heat.

clue.text: An erstwhile entertainer

parts.note: per means 'an' or 'each', as in so much per head
former means erstwhile, of an earlier time

explanation.surface: A one-time showman, now retired.
explanation.walkthrough: PER is 'an' as in a pound an hour, a pound per hour.
explanation.definitionFit: A performer is an artiste who entertains an audience on stage.

clue.text: Wicket maybe taking your spin

indicators.note: taking means the outer word takes the other letters inside itself

parts.note: a wicket is a small gate, hence the 'maybe'

explanation.surface: Cricket: a wicket perhaps falling to your spin bowling.
explanation.walkthrough: The cricket surface hides that a wicket is also a small gate or door.
explanation.definitionFit: To gyrate is to rotate or whirl around a central point.

clue.text: No touching, fellow states on far side of pool

parts.note: re means concerning or touching on
USA is the United States

indicators.note: far side of means the last letter of the word

parts.note: last letter of pool

explanation.surface: A sign by a swimming pool: no touching, and the guy points to the States across the water.
explanation.definitionFit: A refusal is a negative answer, a declining of a request.
